Preparation of Porous Electrospun Fibers with Loaded HNC Matrimid (Matrimid) was provided by Huntsman Advanced Materials. Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) with molecular weight of 400,000 Da was purchased from Sigma-Aldrich. The solvents methanol (CH OH, 99.8%) and dichloromethane (CH Cl , 99.5%) were purchased from Fischer- 3 2 2 Scientific. Fabrication of the fibers was based on previous literature reports that created sorbents embedded in porous electrospun fibers.21,22 The fabrication process was shown schematically in Figure 7. 11 Figure 7. Schematic showing the process of fabricating porous electrospun fibers. SPAR: solvothermal polymer additive removal; ENNC: electrospun nanofiber/nanoparticle composites. Fibers were electrospun in CH Cl solutions in different mass ratios of Matrimid: PEO: 2 2 sorbent. Sorbent was suspended in polymeric solutions, and a custom-designed electrospinning apparatus, as shown in Figure 8, was used for electrospinning. Electrospinning solutions were loaded into a syringe for electrospinning. The fibers were deposited on the aluminum sheets and parameters of the voltage, collector plate distance, and flow rate were varied to gain an understanding of how to operate the equipment. Ranges of variables included flow rates between 0.05 and 0.2 mL/min, voltages between 10 and 25 kV, and working distances between 5 and 20 cm with aluminum foil as the grounded collector. To wash samples, fibers were immersed in 15 mL methanol solutions and heated to 65°C for 12 h, until they were within 5% of the expected mass, considering complete PEO removal. Samples were activated at 45°C under vacuum for 100 h before further tests. Figure 8. Picture of a custom-designed electrospinning apparatus. 2.3. Characterization of Sorbents 2.3.1. General Characterization The surface and cross-sectional morphology of HNC and PEF were characterized by Focused Ion Beam Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB-SEM)-Carl Zeiss AURIGA. Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM, JEOL 2010F, 200 kV) was also used to characterize coating morphology. Samples dispersed in ethanol were deposited on lacey carbon copper grids and dried before imaging. Coating presence and thickness were assessed from multiple images. Fourier-transform 12 Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR, BRUKER VERTEX 70) was performed to investigate the PA-coated sorbents.
